records.source: תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֜ר בְּצִיּ֗וֹן וְהָרִ֨יעוּ֙ בְּהַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֔י יִרְגְּז֕וּ כֹּ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־בָ֥א יוֹם־יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֥י קָרֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Blow a ram's horn in Zion, and sound an alarm on my holy mountain! Let tremble all [the] inhabitants of the land, for [is] coming [the] day of Yahweh, for near [it is].
pieces: Blow the ram's horn in Zion! \q Sound the battle alarm on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain! \q Let everyone who lives in the land tremble, \q for the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is on its way; it is close at hand.

L.1: Blow a trumpet in Zion; \q raise the alarm on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain! \q Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, \q because the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} comes; it is near indeed.

R.1: Blow the trumpet in Zion! \q Sound the alarm on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain! \q Everyone who lives in the land should tremble with fear, \q because the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming. It is very near.

decisions.choice: the ram's horn and the alarm: the signal that an enemy is coming
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown, and a loud signal raised, to warn a city of attack and call it to arms (Numbers 10:9; Jeremiah 4:5; Hosea 5:8; Amos 3:6). The watchman on Zion is to sound it because an army is coming (verses 2-11).

decisions.choice: my holy mountain: the LORD speaks of Zion as his
decisions.reason: Zion, the hill of the temple in Jerusalem, is the LORD's holy mountain (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 11:9; Joel 4:17). The "my" shows that the LORD gives the order, though the prophet goes on to speak of him in the third person.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD is coming: now as an army against Zion
decisions.reason: The day announced in 1:15 now comes as an army that attacks Jerusalem itself (see the note at 1:15). The LORD leads it (verse 11).

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The shofar, a ram's horn, follows the wording set in Isaiah when it stands alone: "trumpet" at Literal and Readable, "ram's horn" at Balanced. Balanced says "battle alarm" for the war signal.

records.heading: The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and its army

records.source: י֧וֹם חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וַאֲפֵלָ֗ה י֤וֹם עָנָן֙ וַעֲרָפֶ֔ל כְּשַׁ֖חַר פָּרֻ֣שׂ עַל־הֶֽהָרִ֑ים עַ֚ם רַ֣ב וְעָצ֔וּם כָּמֹ֗הוּ לֹ֤א נִֽהְיָה֙ מִן־הָ֣עוֹלָ֔ם וְאַֽחֲרָיו֙ לֹ֣א יוֹסֵ֔ף עַד־שְׁנֵ֖י דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness! Like dawn spread over the mountains, a people great and mighty; like it there has not been from of old, and after it will not be again until [the] years of generation and generation.
pieces: It is a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and deep darkness. \q Like the dawn spreading across the mountains \q comes a great and mighty people. \q Nothing like it has ever been before, \q and nothing like it will ever be again \q through all the generations to come.

L.2: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness! \q Like dawn spread out on the mountains, \q a people great and mighty; \q its like has never been from of old, \q and after it there will not be again \q through the years of generation upon generation.

R.2: It will be a dark and gloomy day, a day of black clouds. \q Like the first light of morning spreading across the mountains, \q a huge and powerful army is coming. \q There has never been anything like it before, \q and there will never be anything like it again, \q not for many, many years.

decisions.choice: darkness and gloom, cloud and thick darkness: the darkness of the LORD's coming
decisions.reason: The same four words describe the day of the LORD in Zephaniah 1:15, and cloud and thick darkness surrounded the LORD on Sinai (Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:22). A swarm of locusts darkened the land of Egypt (Exodus 10:15). The darkness here is both: the swarm that blots out the sun, and the day of the LORD it announces.

decisions.choice: like dawn spread over the mountains: the army spreads as fast and far as the first light
alternatives: like blackness spread over the mountains
decisions.reason: The army covers the hills as quickly and widely as dawn spreads across them. Some read a word with almost the same letters, "blackness", which would match the darkness of the first line, but the Hebrew has "dawn".

decisions.choice: nothing like it before or after: as the locusts of Egypt
decisions.reason: Exodus 10:14 says of the locust plague in Egypt that there had never been such a swarm before, nor would there be again. Joel uses the same kind of words for the army now coming.

decisions.choice: a great and mighty people: the locust army, as in 1:6
decisions.reason: As in 1:6, the swarm is called a "people" and described as an army. In verse 11 it is named as the LORD's own army, and in 2:25 he calls the locusts "my great army".

decisions.choice: army (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" for "people", which is the picture the verses develop (m4).

records.source: לְפָנָיו֙ אָ֣כְלָה אֵ֔שׁ וְאַחֲרָ֖יו תְּלַהֵ֣ט לֶֽהָבָ֑ה כְּגַן־עֵ֨דֶן הָאָ֜רֶץ לְפָנָ֗יו וְאַֽחֲרָיו֙ מִדְבַּ֣ר שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְגַם־פְּלֵיטָ֖ה לֹא־הָ֥יְתָה לּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Before it fire consumes, and after it a flame sets ablaze; like [the] garden of Eden [is] the land before it, and after it a wilderness of desolation; and also escape there is none from it.
pieces: Fire devours in front of them, \q and behind them a flame blazes. \q Ahead of them the land is like the garden of Eden; behind them it is a desolate wilderness; \q nothing escapes them.

L.3: Before it fire devours, \q and behind it a flame burns; \q like the garden of Eden [is] the land before it, and behind it a desolate wilderness, \q and nothing at all escapes it.

R.3: In front of them a fire destroys everything. \q Behind them flames burn everything up. \q Before they come, the land looks like the garden of Eden. After they pass, it is an empty desert. \q Nothing escapes them.

decisions.choice: like the garden of Eden: the promise of Eden turned around
decisions.reason: Eden is the garden God planted (Genesis 2:8-15). The prophets promise that the ruined land will become like Eden (Isaiah 51:3; Ezekiel 36:35). Here the picture is reversed: a land like Eden is left a desert.

decisions.choice: fire and flame: the swarm destroys like fire
decisions.reason: The army leaves the land as bare as if a fire had swept it, as the drought did in 1:19-20. A swarm of locusts can strip a region as completely as fire.

decisions.choice: escape: none escapes it
decisions.reason: The word means what escapes or survives. The same word returns in 3:5, where those who call on the LORD's name escape on Mount Zion.

decisions.choice: them (B, R); it (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the army as "it", one people. Balanced and Readable say "they" and "them", which is natural English for an army or a swarm.

records.source: כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה סוּסִ֖ים מַרְאֵ֑הוּ וּכְפָרָשִׁ֖ים כֵּ֥ן יְרוּצֽוּן׃
records.gloss: Like [the] appearance of horses [is] its appearance, and like war horses, so they run.
pieces: They look like horses; \q like war horses they charge.

L.4: Its appearance [is] like the appearance of horses, \q and like war horses, so they run.

R.4: They look like horses, \q and they run like horses charging into battle.

decisions.choice: like horses: the head of a locust looks like a horse's head
decisions.reason: The resemblance between a locust's head and a horse's is often noticed. Revelation 9:7 takes up the picture: "the locusts were like horses prepared for battle."

decisions.choice: war horses: horses trained for battle
decisions.reason: The word can mean horsemen or the horses they ride. Next to "horses" it is most likely the swift horses of the cavalry.

decisions.choice: They look like horses (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they look like" for "its appearance [is] like the appearance of".

records.source: כְּק֣וֹל מַרְכָּב֗וֹת עַל־רָאשֵׁ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יְרַקֵּד֔וּן כְּקוֹל֙ לַ֣הַב אֵ֔שׁ אֹכְלָ֖ה קָ֑שׁ כְּעַ֣ם עָצ֔וּם עֱר֖וּךְ מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Like [the] sound of chariots on [the] tops of the mountains they leap, like [the] sound of a flame of fire consuming stubble, like a people mighty, arrayed for battle.
pieces: With a noise like chariots they leap over the mountaintops, \q like the crackling of a blazing fire that burns up stubble, \q like a mighty army lined up for battle.

L.5: Like the sound of chariots on the tops of the mountains they leap, \q like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, \q like a mighty people drawn up for battle.

R.5: They leap over the mountaintops with a noise like rumbling chariots. \q They sound like a fire roaring through dry stalks. \q They are like a strong army ready for battle.

decisions.choice: the sound of chariots: the roar of a swarm on the move
decisions.reason: A great swarm of locusts makes a loud roaring and crackling sound that can be heard from far away. Revelation 9:9 says of its locusts that the noise of their wings was like the noise of many chariots rushing into battle.

decisions.choice: stubble: dry stalks left in the field
decisions.reason: Stubble burns fast and loudly. It is used for what fire consumes in an instant (Isaiah 5:24; Obadiah 18).

decisions.choice: army (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" for "people", as Readable does in verse 2.

records.source: מִפָּנָ֖יו יָחִ֣ילוּ עַמִּ֑ים כָּל־פָּנִ֖ים קִבְּצ֥וּ פָארֽוּר׃
records.gloss: Before it are in anguish peoples; all faces gather a glow.
pieces: At the sight of them nations writhe in anguish; \q every face turns pale.

L.6: Before it peoples writhe in anguish; \q all faces grow pale.

R.6: When the people of the nations see them, they shake with fear. \q Every face turns pale.

decisions.choice: all faces grow pale: they lose their color in fear
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "gather a glow", is found again only in Nahum 2:11. It most likely means that the faces draw in their color and turn pale. Some take it the other way: the faces flush red with fear.

decisions.choice: writhe in anguish: the word for the pains of childbirth
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a woman in labor and of people seized by terror (Isaiah 13:8; Jeremiah 4:31).

decisions.choice: At the sight of them (B); When the people of the nations see them (R)
decisions.reason: "Before it" means at its approach. Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: כְּגִבּוֹרִ֣ים יְרֻצ֔וּן כְּאַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה יַעֲל֣וּ חוֹמָ֑ה וְאִ֤ישׁ בִּדְרָכָיו֙ יֵֽלֵכ֔וּן וְלֹ֥א יְעַבְּט֖וּן אֹרְחוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Like warriors they run; like men of war they go up a wall; and each in his ways they go, and not they change their paths.
pieces: They charge like warriors; \q they scale the wall like soldiers. \q Each one marches straight ahead; \q none of them breaks rank.

L.7: Like warriors they run; \q like men of war they climb the wall; \q each one goes on its own way, \q and they do not swerve from their paths.

R.7: They run like warriors. \q They climb walls like soldiers. \q Each one marches straight ahead, \q and none of them gets out of line.

decisions.choice: they do not swerve: they do not turn aside from their paths
decisions.reason: The verb, as the Hebrew text has it, elsewhere means to take a pledge. Here it must mean something like turn aside or change course, which fits the parallel line; the ancient translations understood it so. The swarm keeps perfect order, like a disciplined army.

decisions.choice: the wall: a city wall
decisions.reason: Locusts climb over walls and into houses (Exodus 10:6). Verse 9 shows the army taking a city.

decisions.choice: each one ... its (L); Each one (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "each man", the usual way to say "each". Since the army is of locusts, every level says "each one", and Literal says "its" for "his".

records.source: וְאִ֤ישׁ אָחִיו֙ לֹ֣א יִדְחָק֔וּן גֶּ֥בֶר בִּמְסִלָּת֖וֹ יֵֽלֵכ֑וּן וּבְעַ֥ד הַשֶּׁ֛לַח יִפֹּ֖לוּ לֹ֥א יִבְצָֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And each his brother they do not jostle; each man in his path they go; and through the weapons they fall, not they break off.
pieces: They do not push one another; \q each marches in its own track. \q They plunge through the weapons and do not stop.

L.8: They do not jostle one another; \q each goes in its own track; \q they plunge through the weapons and are not halted.

R.8: They do not bump into each other. \q Each one goes straight ahead. \q Weapons cannot stop them as they rush forward.

decisions.choice: they plunge through the weapons and are not halted
alternatives: they plunge through the water channels and are not cut off
decisions.reason: The word for "weapons" names a thrown weapon such as a javelin, and the line pictures the swarm plunging through the defenders' missiles without being stopped. The same word can mean a water channel, and the last verb can mean "be cut off" or "be wounded", so the line could also mean that they go down through the channels and are not cut off. The sense is clear either way: nothing stops them.

decisions.choice: each his brother, each man: each one of the swarm
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the words "brother" and "man" to say "one another" and "each". The subject is still the locust army.

decisions.choice: one another, each, its (all levels)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the words "brother" and "man" are given as "one another" and "each", and Literal says "its" for "his".

records.source: בָּעִ֣יר יָשֹׁ֗קּוּ בַּֽחוֹמָה֙ יְרֻצ֔וּן בַּבָּתִּ֖ים יַעֲל֑וּ בְּעַ֧ד הַחַלּוֹנִ֛ים יָבֹ֖אוּ כַּגַּנָּֽב׃
records.gloss: On the city they rush; on the wall they run; into the houses they go up; through the windows they enter like a thief.
pieces: They swarm over the city; they run along the wall; \q they climb into the houses; \q they come in through the windows like a thief.

L.9: They rush upon the city; they run on the wall; \q they climb into the houses; \q through the windows they enter like a thief.

R.9: They rush into the city and run along the walls. \q They climb into the houses. \q They come in through the windows like thieves.

decisions.choice: windows: openings in the wall, with lattices but no glass
decisions.reason: Windows in houses of the time were openings closed with wooden lattice, not glass. Nothing keeps the swarm out (Exodus 10:6).

decisions.choice: like a thief: unannounced and unstoppable
decisions.reason: A thief comes in where no one expects. The New Testament uses the same picture for the coming of the day of the Lord (1 Thessalonians 5:2; 2 Peter 3:10).

decisions.choice: thieves (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural to match "they".

records.source: לְפָנָיו֙ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֔רֶץ רָעֲשׁ֖וּ שָׁמָ֑יִם שֶׁ֤מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֨חַ֙ קָדָ֔רוּ וְכוֹכָבִ֖ים אָסְפ֥וּ נָגְהָֽם׃
records.gloss: Before it trembles [the] earth; shake [the] heavens; sun and moon become dark, and stars withdraw their brightness.
pieces: Before them the earth quakes \q and the sky shakes; \q the sun and moon go dark, \q and the stars lose their brightness.

L.10: Before it the earth trembles; \q the heavens shake; \q the sun and the moon grow dark, \q and the stars withdraw their shining.

R.10: The earth shakes in front of them, \q and the sky trembles. \q The sun and the moon become dark, \q and the stars stop shining.

decisions.choice: the earth quakes and the lights of the sky go dark: the signs of the LORD's coming
decisions.reason: When the LORD comes, the earth shakes and the heavens tremble (Judges 5:4; Psalm 18:8; Isaiah 13:10, 13). A swarm can blot out the sun, but the words go beyond the locusts: the day of the LORD itself is here. The second half of the verse returns word for word in 4:15, and 3:4 speaks of the sun and moon in the same way.

decisions.choice: before it: at the army's approach
decisions.reason: The "it" is the army of verses 2-9. In the next verse the LORD himself is at its head.

decisions.choice: the sky (B, R); the heavens (L)
decisions.reason: The word means both the sky and heaven. Balanced and Readable say "the sky", set against the earth. The same wording is used in 4:15.

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן קוֹלוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י חֵיל֔וֹ כִּ֣י רַ֤ב מְאֹד֙ מַחֲנֵ֔הוּ כִּ֥י עָצ֖וּם עֹשֵׂ֣ה דְבָר֑וֹ כִּֽי־גָד֧וֹל יוֹם־יְהוָ֛ה וְנוֹרָ֥א מְאֹ֖ד וּמִ֥י יְכִילֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh gives his voice before his army; for very great [is] his camp; for mighty [is the one] doing his word; for great [is the] day of Yahweh and very fearful, and who can endure it?
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thunders at the head of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} forces are vast, \q and mighty is the one who carries out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command. \q The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is great and very terrible. Who can endure it?

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} utters {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army, \q for very great is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} camp, \q for mighty is the one who does {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word; \q for great [is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and very fearful, and who can endure it?

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} shouts out orders to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army. \q There are so many soldiers in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army! \q Those who obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands are very strong. \q The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is great and terrible. Who can live through it?

decisions.choice: the LORD's army: the LORD himself leads the invaders
decisions.reason: The army of verses 2-10 is the LORD's own, and he leads it. In 2:25 he calls the locusts "my great army, which I sent among you". The disaster is his judgment, so only turning to him can avert it (verses 12-14).

decisions.choice: gives his voice: thunders, or shouts his command
decisions.reason: To "give one's voice" is to shout or roar; with God as subject it often means thunder (Psalm 18:14; 46:7). Here it is the battle cry of a commander at the head of his army. 4:16 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: mighty is the one who does his word: the army that carries out his command
alternatives: the LORD, who carries out his word
decisions.reason: The one who "does his word" is the army, carrying out the LORD's order (compare Psalm 103:20). The phrase could also describe the LORD, who carries out what he has said.

decisions.choice: great and very fearful, and who can endure it?
decisions.reason: The day is "great and fearful" again in 3:4 and Malachi 3:23. Malachi 3:2 asks the same question: "who can endure the day of his coming?"

decisions.choice: fearful (L); terrible (B, R); thunders (B)
decisions.reason: The word means "to be feared". Literal says "fearful", Balanced and Readable "terrible", the same at 3:4. Balanced says "thunders" for "gives his voice" (m2), as at 4:16; Readable says he shouts orders.

records.source: וְגַם־עַתָּה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה שֻׁ֥בוּ עָדַ֖י בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וּבְצ֥וֹם וּבְבְכִ֖יוּבְמִסְפֵּֽד׃
records.gloss: And even now, declaration of Yahweh, return to me with all your heart, and with fasting and with weeping and with mourning.
pieces: Yet even now, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all your heart, \q with fasting and weeping and mourning.

L.12: And even now, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all your heart, \q with fasting, and with weeping, and with lamenting.

R.12: But even now, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all your heart. \q Go without food, weep, and mourn.

decisions.choice: return to me with all your heart: turn back to God in repentance
decisions.reason: To "return" is to turn back to God after turning away from him. Deuteronomy 4:30 and 30:2, 10 promise that if the people return to the LORD with all their heart, he will have compassion on them. Joel names no particular sin; the call is for a whole-hearted return.

decisions.choice: yet even now: though the day is near, it is not too late
decisions.reason: After the terror of verses 1-11, the LORD himself speaks. Even with the army at the gates there is still time to turn.

decisions.choice: fasting, weeping and mourning: the signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: These were the outward acts of people who humbled themselves before God, as in the fast called in 1:14. Verse 13 says what must go with them.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (L, B); says the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula follows the wording set in Isaiah. The LORD's own words take no quotation marks.

records.source: וְקִרְע֤וּ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַל־בִּגְדֵיכֶ֔ם וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ ה֔וּא אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And tear your heart and not your garments, and return to Yahweh your God; for gracious and compassionate [is] he, long of anger and great of loyal love, and relenting over the evil.
pieces: Tear your hearts, not your clothes, \q and turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is gracious and full of tender compassion, \q slow to grow angry and rich in loyal love, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} relents from sending disaster.

L.13: And tear your heart and not your clothes, \q and return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q for gracious and compassionate [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, \q long of anger and great in loyal love, \q and relenting over disaster.

R.13: Do not just tear your clothes to show your sorrow. Let your hearts be torn. \q Come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. \q He is kind and full of tender mercy. \q He is slow to become angry, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is great. \q He is ready to change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind and not send disaster.

decisions.choice: tear your heart and not your garments: inward sorrow, not only its outward sign
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the usual sign of grief or horror (Genesis 37:34; 2 Kings 22:11). The prophet does not forbid it, but asks for what it was meant to show: a heart broken over sin.

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in loyal love: the words the LORD proclaimed to Moses
decisions.reason: These words come from Exodus 34:6, where the LORD tells Moses his name and what he is like. They are repeated through Scripture (Numbers 14:18; Psalm 103:8; 145:8; Nehemiah 9:17). Joel, like Jonah 4:2, puts "gracious" first, leaves out "and faithfulness", and adds "and relenting over disaster". The reason to return is who the LORD has shown himself to be.

decisions.choice: relenting over disaster: willing to hold back the harm he has threatened
decisions.reason: To "relent" is to change one's mind and hold back what was planned. The LORD relented from the disaster he had threatened against Israel at Sinai (Exodus 32:12, 14), and he promises to relent when a nation turns from its evil (Jeremiah 18:8; compare Amos 7:3, 6). The word for "disaster" is the common word for evil, here meaning harm, not wrongdoing, as in Jeremiah 4:6.

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 34:6 at each level, with hesed as loyal love (L, B) and faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: Where Joel quotes Exodus 34:6, each level reuses the published wording: "compassionate and gracious", "long of anger" and "great in" (L); "tender compassion" and "slow to grow angry" (B); "tender mercy", "kindness", "slow to become angry" and "his faithful love is great" (R). Joel's order, "gracious" first, is kept at Literal and Balanced. The word hesed follows the wording set for the prophets: "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced, where Exodus has "steadfast love" and "faithful love", and "faithful love" at Readable, as Exodus.

decisions.choice: Do not just tear your clothes to show your sorrow. Let your hearts be torn.
decisions.reason: Readable explains why people tore their clothes (m1) and puts the command for the heart second, so that the contrast is clear.

records.source: מִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ יָשׁ֣וּב וְנִחָ֑ם וְהִשְׁאִ֤יר אַֽחֲרָיו֙ בְּרָכָ֔ה מִנְחָ֣ה וָנֶ֔סֶךְ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: Who knows? He will turn and relent, and leave behind him a blessing, a grain offering and a drink offering for Yahweh your God.
pieces: Who knows? He may turn back and relent, \q and leave behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a blessing: \q grain offerings and drink offerings \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.14: Who knows [whether] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn and relent, \q and leave behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a blessing, \q a grain offering and a drink offering \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?

R.14: Who knows? Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind and not punish you. \q Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will leave you a blessing. \q Then you will have grain and wine to offer \q to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: who knows?: hope that does not presume on God
decisions.reason: The same words are spoken by the king of Nineveh (Jonah 3:9) and by David (2 Samuel 12:22). The people cannot force God's hand; they turn to him and hope in his mercy.

decisions.choice: leave behind him a blessing: as he turns back, he leaves a harvest behind
decisions.reason: The LORD is pictured as turning around and leaving a blessing in his tracks, where the locusts left ruin. The blessing is enough grain and wine for the offerings of 1:9 and 1:13 to be made again.

decisions.choice: change his mind and not punish you; grain and wine to offer
decisions.reason: Readable says what "turn and relent" means here (see verse 13) and what the grain offering and drink offering are made of.

records.source: תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּצִיּ֑וֹן קַדְּשׁוּ־צ֖וֹם קִרְא֥וּ עֲצָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Blow a ram's horn in Zion; consecrate a fast; call an assembly.
pieces: Blow the ram's horn in Zion! \q Proclaim a holy fast; call a solemn assembly.

L.15: Blow a trumpet in Zion; \q set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly.

R.15: Blow the trumpet in Zion! \q Announce a holy fast, a time to go without food. Call everyone to a special meeting.

decisions.choice: the trumpet of 2:1 and the fast of 1:14, now together
decisions.reason: The first words repeat 2:1, the rest repeat 1:14. The trumpet that sounded the alarm of war now calls the people to the fast and assembly of repentance.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B); the wording of 1:14 for the fast
decisions.reason: The shofar, a ram's horn, follows the wording set in Isaiah when it stands alone: "trumpet" at Literal and Readable, "ram's horn" at Balanced. The call to the fast and the assembly uses the wording of 1:14 at each level.

records.heading: The people gather, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answers

records.source: אִסְפוּ־עָ֞ם קַדְּשׁ֤וּ קָהָל֙ קִבְצ֣וּ זְקֵנִ֔ים אִסְפוּ֙ עֽוֹלָלִ֔ים וְיֹנְקֵ֖י שָׁדָ֑יִם יֵצֵ֤א חָתָן֙ מֵֽחֶדְר֔וֹ וְכַלָּ֖ה מֵחֻפָּתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Gather [the] people; consecrate [the] congregation; assemble [the] elders; gather [the] children and those sucking [the] breasts; let go out [the] bridegroom from his room and [the] bride from her chamber.
pieces: Gather the people; make the assembly holy; bring together the elders; \q gather the children, \q even babies nursing at the breast. \q Let the bridegroom leave his own room \q and the bride her wedding chamber.

L.16: Gather the people; consecrate the congregation; assemble the elders; \q gather the children, \q even infants at the breast; \q let the bridegroom come out of his room, \q and the bride out of her chamber.

R.16: Bring all the people together. Prepare them for the holy meeting. Gather the elders, \q the children, and even the babies who are still nursing. \q Let the bridegroom and the bride leave their rooms and come too.

decisions.choice: consecrate the congregation: prepare the people to come before God
decisions.reason: Before meeting God the people made themselves ritually clean, washing their clothes and keeping apart from what made them unclean, including sexual relations (Exodus 19:10, 14-15). This may be why even the newly married are called.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom and the bride: not even the newly married are excused
decisions.reason: A newly married man was freed from going to war or other duties for a year (Deuteronomy 24:5). No one is excused from this assembly. The word for the bride's "chamber" is used of the wedding canopy or room (Psalm 19:6).

decisions.choice: everyone, from the elders to the nursing babies
decisions.reason: The list runs from the oldest to the youngest, the whole people with no exception, as in the call of 1:14.

decisions.choice: Let the bridegroom and the bride leave their rooms and come too.
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two lines about the bridegroom and the bride and says why they leave: to come to the assembly.

records.source: בֵּ֤ין הָאוּלָם֙ וְלַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ יִבְכּוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְֽיֹאמְר֞וּ ח֧וּסָה יְהוָ֣ה עַל־עַמֶּ֗ךָ וְאַל־תִּתֵּ֨ן נַחֲלָתְךָ֤ לְחֶרְפָּה֙ לִמְשָׁל־בָּ֣ם גּוֹיִ֔ם לָ֚מָּה יֹאמְר֣וּ בָֽעַמִּ֔ים אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Between the porch and the altar let weep the priests, ministers of Yahweh, and let them say, Spare, Yahweh, your people, and do not give your inheritance to reproach, to a byword among them, nations. Why should they say among the peoples, Where [is] their God?
pieces: Between the porch and the altar \q let the priests weep, \q those who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Let them pray, "Have pity on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Do not let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance become a disgrace, a byword among the nations. \q Why should the peoples be allowed to say, \q 'Where is their God?'"

L.17: Between the porch and the altar \q let the priests weep, \q the ministers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and let them say, "Spare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance a reproach, a byword among the nations. \q Why should it be said among the peoples, \q 'Where [is] their God?'"

R.17: The priests who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} should weep \q between the altar and the entrance to the temple. \q They should pray, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have pity on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. Do not let other nations make fun of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people and use their name as an insult. \q Why should the nations be able to say, 'Where is their God?'"

decisions.choice: between the porch and the altar: in the court of the temple, where the priests stood
decisions.reason: The porch was the entrance hall at the front of the temple, and the great altar of burnt offering stood in the courtyard before it. The space between them was the priests' place (Ezekiel 8:16; Matthew 23:35).

decisions.choice: your inheritance: Israel, the people the LORD has made his own
decisions.reason: An inheritance is a family's own land, held for good. Moses prayed with the same words, "do not destroy your people, your inheritance" (Deuteronomy 9:26, 29).

decisions.choice: a byword among the nations: a people whose name others use in mockery
alternatives: so that the nations rule over them
decisions.reason: The word, as the Hebrew is pointed, is a verb meaning "to rule", and the line can be read "so that the nations rule over them". Next to "reproach", and with 2:19 answering "I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations", it is read here as the noun for a proverb or byword: a people mocked by others (Deuteronomy 28:37; Jeremiah 24:9).

decisions.choice: "Where is their God?": the taunt of the nations
decisions.reason: The same taunt is heard in Psalm 79:10 and 115:2 and Micah 7:10. If God's people are left in ruin, the nations will say that their God could not or would not help them. The priests appeal to God's concern for his own name.

decisions.choice: Have pity on (B, R); Spare (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to look on with pity and spare. Balanced and Readable say "have pity on". The priests' prayer takes double quotation marks, and the nations' words inside it take single ones.

decisions.choice: make fun of your people and use their name as an insult
decisions.reason: Readable explains "a reproach, a byword" (m3).

records.source: וַיְקַנֵּ֥א יְהוָ֖ה לְאַרְצ֑וֹ וַיַּחְמֹ֖ל עַל־עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh became jealous for his land and had pity on his people.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became jealous for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land \q and took pity on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.18: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became jealous for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land \q and had pity on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.18: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed how deeply {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cared for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had pity on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: then the LORD became jealous: the turning point of the book
alternatives: a promise: the LORD will become jealous
decisions.reason: The verbs are the ones Hebrew uses to tell what happened next. The people did what the LORD asked, and he answered (verse 19). From here on the book is promise. Some read the verbs as a promise of what the LORD will do, but the Hebrew forms most naturally tell of what he did.

decisions.choice: jealous: the LORD's passionate, protective love for what is his
decisions.reason: The word describes a strong love that will not let what belongs to it be harmed or taken. With the LORD as subject it is often turned against his enemies on behalf of his people (Zechariah 1:14; 8:2; Isaiah 9:6).

decisions.choice: had pity: the same verb as "spare" in the priests' prayer
decisions.reason: The priests prayed, "Spare your people" (verse 17), and the LORD "spared", had pity on, his people. The answer uses the words of the prayer.

decisions.choice: showed how deeply he cared for (R)
decisions.reason: Readable avoids "jealous", which in everyday English suggests envy, and says what the word means here (m2).

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעַמּ֗וֹ הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֤חַ לָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַדָּגָן֙ וְהַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר וּשְׂבַעְתֶּ֖ם אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹא־אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶתְכֶ֥ם ע֛וֹד חֶרְפָּ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh answered and said to his people, Here I am sending to you the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and you will be satisfied with it; and I will not make you again a reproach among the nations.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and said: I am sending you grain, new wine, and olive oil, \q and you will have all you want. \q Never again will I make you a disgrace among the nations.

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: Look, I am sending you the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil, \q and you will be satisfied with it; \q and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He said: I am sending you grain, wine, and olive oil. \q You will have plenty to eat and drink. \q I will never again let the other nations make fun of you.

decisions.choice: the LORD answered: his answer runs on to the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: The LORD now speaks in the first person, answering the prayer of verse 17. His words run through verse 27, and the promises of chapter 3 continue in his voice.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and fresh oil: the losses of 1:10 restored
decisions.reason: The three products lost in 1:10 are given back, as in the promise of Hosea 2:24.

decisions.choice: no longer a reproach among the nations: the priests' prayer answered word for word
decisions.reason: The priests asked that the LORD's people not be made "a reproach" among the nations (verse 17). The LORD promises exactly that.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for the LORD's words
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the prophets, the LORD's own words take no quotation marks; a colon introduces them. The answer runs on through several verses (m1). Readable says "wine" for "new wine" and "olive oil" for "fresh oil", as Hosea 2:10.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־הַצְּפוֹנִ֞י אַרְחִ֣יק מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֗ם וְהִדַּחְתִּיו֮ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צִיָּ֣ה וּשְׁמָמָה֒ אֶת־פָּנָ֗יו אֶל־הַיָּם֙ הַקַּדְמֹנִ֔י וְסֹפ֖וֹ אֶל־הַיָּ֣ם הָאַֽחֲר֑וֹן וְעָלָ֣ה בָאְשׁ֗וֹ וְתַ֨עַל֙ צַחֲנָת֔וֹ כִּ֥י הִגְדִּ֖יל לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And the northerner I will remove far from you, and I will drive it into a land dry and desolate, its front into the eastern sea and its rear into the western sea; and its stench will go up, and its foul smell will rise; for it has done great things.
pieces: I will drive the northern army far away from you, into a dry and desolate land, \q its vanguard into the eastern sea, \q and its rear into the western sea. \q Its stench will rise; its rotting smell will go up, \q for it has done great harm.

L.20: The northerner I will remove far from you and drive into a land dry and desolate, \q its front into the eastern sea, \q and its rear into the western sea; \q its stench will go up, and its foul smell will rise, \q for it has done great things.

R.20: I will drive the army from the north far away from you, into a dry and empty land. \q Some of them will go into the Dead Sea in the east, \q and the rest into the Mediterranean Sea in the west. \q Their dead bodies will rot and stink, \q because of all the harm they have done.

decisions.choice: the northerner: the invading army, called by the name of the enemy from the north
alternatives: a human army from the north
decisions.reason: Invaders from Mesopotamia came into Israel from the north, and the prophets speak of the coming enemy as the one "from the north" (Jeremiah 1:14; 4:6; Ezekiel 38:6, 15). Locusts usually came from the south or east, so the name may be given to the locust army as the feared enemy of the prophets, or it may mean a human army that the locusts foreshadow.

decisions.choice: the eastern sea and the western sea: the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: These are the borders of the land to the east and west (Zechariah 14:8). The "dry and desolate land" between them is most likely the wilderness of Judah. Swarms of locusts driven by the wind into the sea die, and their bodies rot on the shore with a terrible smell; in Egypt a wind drove the locusts into the Red Sea (Exodus 10:19).

decisions.choice: for it has done great things: the enemy has acted proudly and done great harm
alternatives: the LORD has done great things
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in verse 21, where the LORD "has done great things". Here the subject is most likely the northerner: it has done great harm and acted proudly, and so it is destroyed. Some take the line with what follows, so that the LORD is the one who has done great things.

decisions.choice: the northern army (B); the army from the north (R); the Dead Sea, the Mediterranean Sea (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" (m1). Readable names the two seas (m2) and says "great harm" for the sense of "great things" here (m3), as Balanced does.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽירְאִ֖י אֲדָמָ֑ה גִּ֣ילִי וּשְׂמָ֔חִי כִּֽי־הִגְדִּ֥יל יְהוָ֖ה לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: Do not fear, land; be glad and rejoice, for Yahweh has done great things.
pieces: Do not be afraid, O land! \q Be glad and rejoice, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done great things!

L.21: Do not fear, O land; \q be glad and rejoice, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done great things.

R.21: Land, do not be afraid! \q Be glad and full of joy, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done great things.

decisions.choice: the LORD has done great things: the answer to the enemy's great deeds
decisions.reason: The same words were used of the enemy at the end of verse 20. The LORD's great deeds overturn the enemy's. Psalm 126:2-3 uses the same words of the return from exile.

decisions.choice: land: the ground that mourned in 1:10
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "the ground" in 1:10, which "mourned". Now it is told to rejoice. Verse 22 speaks to the animals and verse 23 to the people, in the same order of loss as chapter 1.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽירְאוּ֙ בַּהֲמ֣וֹת שָׂדַ֔י כִּ֥י דָשְׁא֖וּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־עֵץ֙ נָשָׂ֣א פִרְי֔וֹ תְּאֵנָ֥ה וָגֶ֖פֶן נָתְנ֥וּ חֵילָֽם׃
records.gloss: Do not fear, animals of [the] field, for have become green [the] pastures of [the] wilderness; for [the] tree has borne its fruit; fig tree and vine have given their strength.
pieces: Do not be afraid, you wild animals, \q for the pastures in the wilderness are turning green. \q The trees are bearing their fruit; \q the fig tree and the vine give their full yield.

L.22: Do not fear, animals of the field, \q for the pastures of the wilderness have turned green; \q for the tree has borne its fruit; \q the fig tree and the vine have given their strength.

R.22: Wild animals, do not be afraid! \q The grasslands are turning green again. \q The trees are producing fruit. \q The fig trees and grapevines are loaded with fruit.

decisions.choice: the losses of chapter 1 reversed
decisions.reason: The wild animals that longed for God (1:20), the burned pastures of the wilderness (1:19-20), and the fig tree and vine (1:7, 12) are each named again, now restored. The verbs describe what the LORD's promise has already begun.

decisions.choice: have given their strength: given their full yield
decisions.reason: The word for "strength" also means wealth or produce. The trees give all they can bear.

decisions.choice: wild animals (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, "animals of the field" are the wild animals.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י צִיּ֗וֹן גִּ֤ילוּ וְשִׂמְחוּ֙ בַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־נָתַ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם אֶת־הַמּוֹרֶ֖ה לִצְדָקָ֑ה וַיּ֣וֹרֶד לָכֶ֗ם גֶּ֛שֶׁם מוֹרֶ֥ה וּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ בָּרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in Yahweh your God, for he has given to you the early rain for righteousness; and he has brought down for you rain, early rain and late rain, in the first.
pieces: People of Zion, be glad; rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! \q He has given you the autumn rain in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness. \q He has poured down rain for you, the autumn rain and the spring rain, as before.

L.23: Children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given to you the early rain for righteousness; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent down rain for you, the early rain and the late rain, as before.

R.23: People of Zion, be glad! Rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! \q He has given you the autumn rain because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is faithful to you. \q He has sent you plenty of rain, the autumn rain and the spring rain, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did before.

decisions.choice: the early rain and the late rain: the autumn and spring rains on which the harvest depended
decisions.reason: The early rain came in autumn, softening the ground for plowing and sowing; the late rain came in spring and filled out the grain before harvest. Both are promised to a faithful people (Deuteronomy 11:14; Jeremiah 5:24; Hosea 6:3).

decisions.choice: for righteousness: given in the LORD's faithfulness, as a sign that he has put things right with his people
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for righteousness. Here it most likely means the LORD's right and faithful dealing with his people, shown in sending the rain: the rain proves that he has turned to them again. It may also mean rain "in the right measure". The word for "early rain" can also mean "teacher", and the phrase has been read as "the teacher of righteousness", as in the Latin Vulgate; some think the community of the Dead Sea Scrolls drew its title "the Teacher of Righteousness" from this phrase or from Hosea 10:12. The rains named in the next line show that rain is meant here.

decisions.choice: as before: the Hebrew says "in the first"
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can mean "at first", "as before", or "in the first month". The first month of the year, in spring, would suit the late rain but not the early rain, so it is read here as "as before", as in the past.

decisions.choice: autumn rain, spring rain (B, R); in his faithfulness (B); because he is faithful to you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the seasons of the two rains (m1). For "for righteousness" they say what it means here, the LORD's faithful dealing with his people (m2). Literal keeps "for righteousness". "Children of Zion" means the people of Zion.

records.source: וּמָלְא֥וּ הַגֳּרָנ֖וֹת בָּ֑ר וְהֵשִׁ֥יקוּ הַיְקָבִ֖ים תִּיר֥וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And will be full the threshing floors [of] grain, and will overflow the vats [with] new wine and fresh oil.
pieces: The threshing floors will be heaped with grain; \q the vats will overflow with new wine and olive oil.

L.24: And the threshing floors will be filled with grain, \q and the vats will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.

R.24: The threshing floors will be piled high with grain. \q The vats will overflow with new wine and olive oil.

decisions.choice: threshing floors and vats: where the grain, wine and oil were gathered
decisions.reason: A threshing floor was a flat open place where grain was beaten out and winnowed. The vats were the basins below a winepress or olive press, into which the juice or oil ran.

decisions.choice: the vats will overflow: the same words return in 4:13
decisions.reason: Here the overflowing vats are the LORD's blessing on his people. In 4:13 the same words picture his judgment on the nations, as a winepress trodden full.

records.source: וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַשָּׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֙ אָכַ֣ל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה הַיֶּ֖לֶק וְהֶחָסִ֣יל וְהַגָּזָ֑ם חֵילִי֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁלַּ֖חְתִּי בָּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will repay to you the years which has eaten the swarming locust, the hopping locust, and the stripping locust, and the cutting locust, my army the great which I sent among you.
pieces: I will make up to you for the years \q that the swarming locust has eaten, \q the hopping locust, the stripping locust, and the cutting locust, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great army \q that I sent against you.

L.25: And I will repay you for the years \q that the swarming locust has eaten, \q the hopping locust, the stripping locust, and the cutting locust, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great army, \q which I sent among you.

R.25: I will give back to you what you lost in the years \q when one swarm of locusts after another ate your crops. \q They were {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great army, \q which I sent against you.

decisions.choice: the four locusts of 1:4, named in a different order
alternatives: four stages in the growth of one kind of locust
decisions.reason: The same four names as in 1:4 come here in a different order: swarming, hopping, stripping, cutting. Whether they are kinds or stages of locust is uncertain (see 1:4); the change of order suggests that they are four names for one plague.

decisions.choice: I will repay you for the years: make good the loss
decisions.reason: The verb is used of paying back what is owed or making good a loss (Exodus 22:4-5). "The years" suggests that the damage lasted more than one season. The LORD will make up for every lost harvest.

decisions.choice: my great army, which I sent: the LORD sent the locusts
decisions.reason: The LORD owns the disaster as his own act of judgment (2:11). The one who sent it is the one who now repays.

decisions.choice: the locust names as in 1:4 (L, B); one swarm of locusts after another (R)
decisions.reason: The names follow 1:4 at Literal and Balanced, in the order this verse gives them. Readable uses the phrase set for these names. "Against you" at Balanced and Readable says the sense of "among you": the army was sent as judgment.

records.source: וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אָכוֹל֙ וְשָׂב֔וֹעַ וְהִלַּלְתֶּ֗ם אֶת־שֵׁ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה עִמָּכֶ֖ם לְהַפְלִ֑יא וְלֹא־יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ עַמִּ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will eat, eating and being satisfied, and you will praise the name of Yahweh your God, who has dealt with you wonderfully; and will not be ashamed my people forever.
pieces: You will eat your fill and be satisfied, \q and you will praise the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q the one who has worked wonders for you. \q Never again will {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people be put to shame.

L.26: You will eat abundantly and be satisfied, \q and will praise the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who has acted wondrously with you; \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will never be put to shame.

R.26: You will have all the food you want, \q and you will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done amazing things for you. \q My people will never again be ashamed.

decisions.choice: you will eat and be satisfied and praise: as Moses promised
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 8:10 says: "You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you." The doubled verbs ("eat, eating") stress the abundance.

decisions.choice: be put to shame: be disgraced and disappointed
decisions.reason: This is the verb used of the farmers in 1:11 ("be ashamed") and the joy that "dried up" in 1:12. What the people suffered then will not happen again.

decisions.choice: forever: never again
decisions.reason: With "not", the phrase means "never". The promise is repeated at the end of verse 27.

decisions.choice: praise the LORD your God (R)
decisions.reason: "The name" of the LORD stands for the LORD himself; Readable says "praise the LORD".

records.source: וִידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֣י בְקֶ֤רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אָ֔נִי וַאֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם וְאֵ֣ין ע֑וֹד וְלֹא־יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ עַמִּ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And you will know that in [the] midst of Israel [am] I, and I [am] Yahweh your God, and there is no other; and will not be ashamed my people forever.
pieces: Then you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, \q that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am your God, and there is no other. \q Never again will {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people be put to shame.

L.27: And you will know that in the midst of Israel [am] I, \q and I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and there is no other; \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will never be put to shame.

R.27: Then you will know that I live among the people of Israel. \q You will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. There is no other God. \q My people will never again be ashamed.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD your God: the knowledge of God that his acts bring
decisions.reason: The LORD's acts make him known (Exodus 6:7; 29:45-46, where he dwells among his people). Ezekiel uses the same kind of words more than sixty times. "There is no other" is the confession of Deuteronomy 4:35 and Isaiah 45:5-6, 18.

decisions.choice: the last line repeats verse 26
decisions.reason: The repeated promise closes the LORD's answer to the people's lament.

decisions.choice: live among the people of Israel; no other God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "live among" for "in the midst of" and supplies "God" to make "there is no other" plain.
